ESH_GAS_UTZ.canonicalName: Uattzy / UAU (legacy E-Shore, GASGAS, EnerMia partyIds)

newEvidence.finding: Uattzy explicitly identifies itself as the public-charging brand of UAU, created from E-Shore, GASGAS and EnerMia. The current website reports more than 3,000 charging points installed and under management in Italy, materially above the 1,198 EVSE represented by the ESH+GAS+UTZ technical partyIds in the stale PUN-derived seed (892+290+16). Therefore those three partyIds are not a complete present-day inventory proxy for the entire Uattzy/UAU managed network.

The February 2026 first-party PDF reported more than 2,400 charging points installed and managed and describes 2,400 quick and fast points for the Poste Italiane project, including more than 1,300 already installed at that time. This confirms that the current technical inventory must be reconciled against post-merger UAU/Uattzy identifiers rather than inferred only from historical ESH/GAS/UTZ counts.

The app exposes the tariff and any additional costs per connector before charging; the FAQ states that prices may vary by delivered power, session duration and stall-occupation time. This remains incompatible with blindly applying the July headline grid to every historical partyId without connector-level/class-level binding.

coverage.decision: Do not expand or merge technical partyId coverage from corporate branding alone. Preserve ESH/GAS/UTZ as a corporate alias group while retaining each technical partyId until PUN/OCPI/app/backend evidence identifies current UAU/Uattzy ownership and connector-level tariffs deterministically.

aliasDecision.action: group for investigation/dedup context only; do not collapse physical identifiers or count additional managed points without inventory evidence

ESH_GAS_UTZ.blockage: First-party corporate evidence proves the E-Shore/GASGAS/EnerMia merger into UAU/Uattzy, but current Uattzy managed-network size substantially exceeds the historical ESH/GAS/UTZ inventory and the FAQ remains connector-specific. Exact current technical ownership and tariff mapping are still missing.
